doc: How the computer duelist answers each prompt. Each row is one method in DuelAi. fallback = what to send if the engine answers MSG_RETRY to the first choice; after a second retry the AI concedes (logged).

rows.rule: Up to 12 actions per turn: activate a spell/effect that isn't a trap card (60% each time offered, never the same effect 3 times in a turn); else Normal Summon the highest-ATK summonable; else Special Summon the first available; else set a trap/spell (ssetable) if any; else go to Battle Phase if in Main 1 and it has a face-up attack monster, else End Phase.
rows.fallback: End Phase (7), or Battle Phase (6) if End Phase is not offered

rows.rule: Attack with each attacker once (highest ATK first); when none left, Main Phase 2 if offered else End Phase. Never activate in battle unless it is the only option.
Pick max(min,1) cards (not more than max), preferring cards controlled by the opponent when the card list has both sides, else the first ones.
rows.fallback: first min cards in list order, or cancel if allowed

rows.rule: Forced: chain index 0. Otherwise activate index 0 with 50% chance when the chain has fewer than 3 links and no own link yet; else pass (-1).
Own zones first: middle monster zone outward (2,1,3,0,4), extra monster zones, spell/trap zones middle outward; first available per 'blocked' bits; repeat for count.
rows.fallback: scan every zone bit in order

rows.rule: Same order as ai_place but on the opponent's side first (disabling/targeting their zones).
rows.fallback: scan every zone bit in order

rows.rule: Face-up attack if allowed, else face-up defense, else face-down defense, else face-down attack.
Choose the lowest-ATK cards (by DuelState) until releaseParam total >= min.
rows.fallback: first cards in list order until total >= min

rows.rule: Take counters from cards in list order until count is reached.
Depth-first search the subsets of cards (must cards always counted) for one meeting the target exactly (mode 0) or at least with no removable card (mode 1), respecting min/max.
Finish (-1) when finishable; else select the first selectable card.
Take the lowest 'count' bits of available.
Evaluate the opcode program (port of is_declarable) over CardDb and declare the first passcode that passes, preferring cards in the opponent's deck.
